data.narrative:
Astrolab is a Series A-stage space and aerospace company that has raised $40M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a competitive universe of 13 peers: 5 public companies (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private firms including SpaceX, Rocket Lab, and Planet Labs. However, narrow peer comparability is limited by the early stage and heterogeneity of the Space & Aerospace sector.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable framework. Using total capital raised ($40M) as a value proxy and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A advancement yields an implied valuation of $80M. This reflects normalized value accretion expected between funding rounds in the sector. The peer-median approach could not be applied; while 14 same-sector peers exist, none meet minimum sample thresholds (need ≥3) when filtered by stage or valuation tier. Public-company P/S anchoring, though the Space & Aerospace median trades at 27.4x revenue across 6 public tickers, cannot be executed without Astrolab's revenue disclosure—standard for private companies.

The triangulation yields a range of $68M–$92M, with $80M as the central estimate. Given reliance on a single method, key uncertainties include Astrolab's actual revenue run-rate, capital efficiency relative to peer cohorts, and near-term funding trajectory. Validation would require revenue visibility or additional private comparables at equivalent maturity.
